description: Hi everyone! My name is Andrea Ruiz, and I'm an Aerospace Engineering student at UNAM (ENES Juriquilla). I'm deeply passionate about space exploration, aerodynamics, space robotics, and building hardware/software integration projects. I enjoy tackling complex engineering problems and turning creative concepts into functional prototypes.
summary:
An interactive aerospace mission simulator crafted by human hands.

In this experience, players step into the boots of an orbital engineer: assembling a real-world CubeSat subsystem by subsystem, balancing mass against mission risk, selecting authentic launch vehicles like Falcon 9, Electron, or Firefly Alpha, and executing a precision gravity-turn ascent across Earth's atmospheric layers into Low Earth Orbit. Once deployed, the mission shifts to Ground Control, where players decode live orbital telemetry inspired by real NASA and NOAA Earth-observation constellations (such as CYGNSS and VIIRS) to pinpoint critical climate disasters and dispatch life-saving aid.

By turning complex orbital mechanics and satellite remote sensing into a tactile, human-crafted journey, we bridge the gap between everyday citizens and the orbital guardians protecting our planet.
details:
Built in Godot Engine 4 using GDScript, our project is a 100% human-crafted aerospace simulator: featuring custom hand-drawn 2D sprites, backgrounds, UI assets, and physics systems, that guides players through the full lifecycle of an Earth-observation CubeSat mission. Players begin in the workshop by assembling eight authentic satellite subsystems (such as the OBC, power distribution, comms board, and payload) while balancing mass against failure risk before selecting a real launch vehicle (Falcon 9, Electron, or Firefly Alpha). They then configure launch force, time-of-day windows, and gravity-turn angles in a 2D physics simulation that models multi-stage fuel burn, planetary gravity, and atmospheric layers up to Low Earth Orbit.

Once deployed, the mission transitions to Ground Control, where players decode procedurally generated telemetry modeled on real NASA and NOAA Earth-observation constellations: including CYGNSS L-band microwave reflectometry for hurricanes, NOAA-20 VIIRS thermal radiometry for wildfires, and InSAR/FIRMS sensors for seismic activity to pinpoint affected regions on a world map and dispatch emergency aid. By balancing authentic aerospace trade-offs with approachable gameplay, our project turns complex orbital mechanics and satellite remote sensing into an intuitive, hands-on educational experience that shows how small satellites protect life on Earth.
